verdict.line: You lose if you trade evenly with Jayce's poke and knockback before level 6; you win if you farm Q stacks, dodge his cooldown windows, and let the lane turn into the extended fight that the measured 51.8% win rate over 2,338 games actually reflects.

brief.thesis: Jayce's kit is built entirely to deny melee range — Hammer stance's Thundering Blow knocks you back and To the Skies! lets him dash in, poke, and disengage, while Cannon stance adds a 600-range Shock Blast — which is why lane advantage sits with him. Nasus has no dash and wins by stacking Siphoning Strike through the poke and using Wither to strip the mobility his kiting depends on, which is exactly why the head-to-head win rate still favors Nasus despite the lane-phase deficit.

theirWindow.when: Jayce in Cannon stance at range
theirWindow.what: He's firing Shock Blast and can send it through his own Acceleration Gate for extra range, speed, and damage — stay out of the lane, let minions soak it, and don't facetank chip damage for no reason.

yourWindow.what: Without Thundering Blow up he has no knockback to create space after you close — land Wither first, then walk him down and commit to the trade since he can't punch you away.

powerCurve.note: Shock Blast poke outranges your Q entirely
Thundering Blow knockback punishes every engage
Wither and R start neutralizing his kiting
Q stacks and lifesteal win extended trades
Full build sustain overwhelms his damage

start.why: Runs 52.3% over 1,760 games and is the 62.6% pick for a reason — the regen and poke-damage block keep you from bleeding HP to Shock Blast and autos while you're still farming Q.

boots.why: Highest-winning boots at 52.6% over 1,162 games — the ability haste shortens Q's already-low cooldown even further and gets Wither back up faster to re-catch his kiting.

core.why: The highest-winning core path (61.6% over 333 games) starts here — the damage, attack speed, and movement spike are what let Nasus actually close distance on a kiting Jayce.
Armor and the attack-speed slow aura blunt his auto-attack and Shock Blast poke, and the ability haste loops Q and Wither faster.
Magic resist blunts Thundering Blow's magic damage, and the heal amp stacks directly onto Soul Eater lifesteal for the extended fights you're trying to reach.

situational.when: jayce or the rest of the enemy team leans on sustained auto-attacks or healing
you need more closing speed to actually catch his kiting before Trinity Force comes online
you want the slow and tempo earlier than Trinity Force's full build timing allows

runes.keystoneWhy: The sustain-on-hit and movement burst on triggering it help you absorb poke damage and reposition out of Thundering Blow's knockback angle without losing tempo.

summoners.why: Highest-winning combo at 52.8% over the sampled games — Flash dodges a committed To the Skies! or punishes a Thundering Blow setup, and Teleport lets a farming, late-scaling Nasus still apply global pressure.

playing.title: Farm Q, don't trade
playing.detail: Every Siphoning Strike that kills a minion permanently raises its damage, so prioritize landing the 8/7/6/5/4s-cooldown Q over contesting Jayce's pokes.

playing.title: Save Wither for engages
playing.detail: Cast W the moment Jayce commits to To the Skies! or goes Cannon stance for Hyper Charge, since it decelerates both his Movement and Attack Speed and kills his ability to kite away afterward.

playing.title: Track Thundering Blow's cooldown
playing.detail: Hammer-stance E knocks you back on a 20/18/16/14/12s cooldown within 240 range — walking up while it's up just resets the trade in his favor.

playing.title: Zone with Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Drop E when Jayce closes to melee range in Cannon stance, since the armor reduction and burn punish him for standing in it.

playing.title: All-in right after level 6
playing.detail: Pair Wither with R (Fury of the Sands) to close the gap before he can reposition — the health drain and range increase are what let you actually catch him.

playing.title: Don't eat free Shock Blasts
playing.detail: Back off when he's in Cannon stance at range, especially after he's fired through his own Acceleration Gate, since that combo hits hardest and farthest.

playing.title: Win through scaling, not lane
playing.detail: The 51.8% head-to-head win rate comes from late-game stats, not lane kills — play patient early and let Trinity Force into Frozen Heart close the gap.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, boots, summoners, and every win-rate or pick-rate figure above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the ability-timing and trade-pattern reasoning layered on top is my own read of the matchup, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Always keep some distance to avoid being punished by Jayce. Focus foremost on raising your [Q] stacks, and try go in for the kill post-level 6 with Unsealed Spellbook + Fury of the Sands [R] when enemy skills are on cooldown.
